memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Three times a year all your men must appear before the Lord your God at the place he will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Tabernacles. No one should appear before the Lord empty-handed: Each of you must bring a gift in proportion to the way the Lord your God has blessed you. - Deut 16:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three times a year the men of Israel were to gather before God, and no one was to come empty-handed. Each was to bring a gift measured by how God had blessed him. God was drawing His people to Himself regularly, and He wanted their coming to be marked by grateful giving.

Notice again that giving is tied to blessing received, not to a rigid amount. The person who had been blessed much brought much; the one blessed less brought accordingly. What mattered was the heart that recognised every good thing came from God's hand.

There is real beauty in this rhythm of appearing before God. It kept the people from drifting into forgetfulness and self-sufficiency. We need the same. Gathering with God's people, bringing our worship and our offerings, keeps our hearts tender and thankful. And we never come to God truly empty-handed, for we bring ourselves, our praise, and lives offered in response to His mercy (Rom 12:1). Above all, we come because Christ first came for us and gave Himself completely. When you gather to worship, come with a heart ready to give, remembering all He has poured into your life. What gift of gratitude can you bring before God today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you come before God ready to give, or only to receive?
2. How does remembering God's blessing shape your worship?
3. What does offering yourself to God look like this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I come before You grateful for all You have given. Receive my worship and my life as an offering of thanks. Amen.
